Brand Heritage:

Duke Kahanamoku was one of the most influential figures associated with Hawaiian culture, competitive swimming, surfing history, and the development of the Aloha shirt. Born in Hawaii, he achieved international recognition as an Olympic gold medalist and later played an important role in introducing surfing and the Hawaiian lifestyle to audiences around the world during the early twentieth century.

The clothing label bearing his name became one of the historically significant brands associated with the early development and popularization of the Aloha shirt. Particularly prominent from the late 1930s through the 1950s, the Duke Kahanamoku label became known for its distinctive tropical prints, relaxed silhouettes, and strong connection to the golden age of vintage Hawaiian shirting.

In Japan, Duke Kahanamoku garments are produced by Toyo Enterprises under official license from Malama Pono Ltd. Drawing from original garments, period catalogs, labels, textile samples, and other archival references, Toyo Enterprises develops both faithful reproductions of historically important Aloha shirts and original designs inspired by the brand's vintage heritage. These garments are produced with close attention to materials, construction, graphics, proportions, and period-informed finishing details, while maintaining the high manufacturing standards associated with Toyo Enterprises.

Historical Reproduction:

This model is a highly accurate reproduction of the vintage short-sleeve "Duke's Pineapple" Aloha shirt originally produced during the early 1950s. The reproduction is based on surviving archival examples and preserves the distinctive pineapple print, classic garment proportions, period-style construction, and vintage-inspired brand labeling associated with the original design.

Rather than simply applying a vintage-style graphic to a modern shirt body, Toyo Enterprises has recreated the garment as a complete historical design. Details such as the open collar, short and boxy body, straight hem, horizontal buttonholes, shell buttons, double-layer back yoke, back pleats, pattern-matched pockets, and archival-style woven neck label contribute to the historically authentic appearance of the finished shirt.

Fit and Silhouette:

The shirt is cut in a classic mid-century Hawaiian-shirt silhouette, with a generously proportioned body and a slightly shorter body length. The chest and upper torso provide ample ease, while the shoulders are shaped to allow comfortable movement without creating an excessively oversized appearance.

The straight-cut side seams and horizontally finished hem create a relaxed, boxy profile characteristic of vintage Aloha shirts from the period. Unlike a modern fitted shirt with a tapered waist and extended shirttail hem, this garment maintains a straighter shape from the chest through the waist. The shorter body length is specifically designed to be worn untucked and helps balance the wider chest measurement.

The resulting fit offers comfortable room through the chest, shoulders, and upper back while maintaining the compact proportions associated with traditional Hawaiian leisure shirts. Its relaxed construction also allows air to circulate more easily around the body, making it particularly suitable for warm-weather wear.

Open-Collar Construction:

The shirt features a traditional open collar constructed without a separate collar stand. This type of collar is designed to lie naturally against the upper chest and form a relaxed V-shaped opening when the top button is left unfastened.

When worn open, the collar creates the easy, informal appearance traditionally associated with Hawaiian shirts. A fabric loop is positioned at the collar edge and can be secured to the uppermost button when a more closed and orderly neckline is preferred. Fastening the loop button brings the collar points closer together and gives the neckline a more structured appearance.

Front Closure and Buttons:

The front is constructed with a full-length button opening and is secured by six buttons, including the button used with the collar loop. The buttons are four-hole white mother-of-pearl buttons made from natural shell.

Because mother-of-pearl is a natural material, each button may display subtle variations in color, luster, surface pattern, and translucency. Their restrained sheen complements the matte surface of the rayon fabric and adds a refined detail without detracting from the all-over print.

The front buttonholes are positioned horizontally across the front placket. This orientation is consistent with the construction specifications of the reproduced vintage design and also helps stabilize the buttons against horizontal tension when the shirt is worn.

Fabric:

The shirt is made from 100% rayon Fujiette, a lightweight woven fabric selected to reproduce the appearance and hand of vintage Hawaiian shirting. The material has a smooth yet slightly dry surface, a subdued matte luster, and a fluid drape that allows the garment to fall naturally around the body.

Unlike a stiff cotton shirting fabric, rayon Fujiette moves easily and develops soft folds and subtle surface variations during wear. These characteristics contribute to the relaxed appearance of the shirt and enhance the visual depth of the printed design.

The lightweight construction makes the fabric comfortable for warm-weather use, while its flowing drape prevents the generously cut body from appearing excessively rigid or bulky. Natural wrinkling may develop with wear, which is an inherent characteristic of the material and contributes to its vintage-inspired appearance.

Straight Hem and Untucked Styling:

The bottom of the shirt is finished with a straight, horizontally cut hem, sometimes referred to as a square hem or square bottom. This construction differs from the curved shirttail hem commonly used on dress shirts intended to be tucked into trousers.

The straight hem allows the shirt to hang evenly when worn untucked and reinforces its relaxed, box-shaped silhouette. The compact body length and clean horizontal hem make the shirt easy to coordinate with jeans, chinos, shorts, or other casual trousers without requiring the garment to be tucked in.

Double-Layer Back Yoke:

The upper back is constructed with a double-layer back yoke. A second layer of fabric is incorporated across the shoulder area to reinforce a portion of the garment that is regularly subjected to tension from arm movement and daily wear.

This layered construction provides additional structural stability across the shoulders while helping the upper back maintain its intended shape. The yoke also creates a defined transition between the shoulder area and the fuller lower back panel.

Back Pleats:

Four shallow pleats are positioned directly below the back yoke, with two pleats placed on each side. These pleats introduce controlled fullness into the upper back without significantly changing the external shape of the garment.

When the arms move forward or outward, the pleats can open slightly to provide additional ease across the shoulder blades and upper back. This construction improves mobility while allowing the shirt to retain a clean, balanced appearance when the wearer is standing naturally.

Pattern-Matched Chest Pockets:

Two patch pockets are positioned on the chest. Each pocket has a softly curved lower edge that complements the rounded forms within the pineapple print.

The pockets are pattern matched to the front body of the shirt. During production, the pocket pieces are individually positioned and cut so that the printed design aligns as closely as possible with the surrounding body panel after sewing.

This process requires more careful fabric placement than standard pocket construction. By visually continuing the print across the pocket edges, the pockets remain less conspicuous and preserve the uninterrupted appearance of the all-over pattern. Minor alignment differences may occur because of the fluid nature of rayon fabric and the individual cutting and sewing process.

Discharge-Printed All-Over Pattern:

The pineapple motif is produced as an all-over pattern using a discharge-printing process. In this method, the base fabric is first dyed, and selected areas of the dyed ground are then chemically discharged to remove or reduce the original color and form the printed design.

Unlike a surface print in which a thick layer of pigment sits on top of the cloth, discharge printing allows the design to become more closely integrated with the fabric itself. This results in a softer hand, reduced surface buildup, and a more natural transition between the printed motif and the background color.

The process gives the artwork a subdued, slightly irregular character that is especially appropriate for reproducing vintage Hawaiian textiles. Small variations in color density or tonal appearance are natural characteristics of this printing method and should not be considered defects.

"Duke's Pineapple" Design:

The printed artwork is based on "Duke's Pineapple," one of the most recognizable and historically important designs associated with the Duke Kahanamoku label. The composition combines stylized pineapple motifs, leaves, and supporting tropical elements in a dense all-over arrangement that gives the shirt a strong visual presence while maintaining a balanced overall pattern.

Pineapple designs occupy an important place in the history of vintage Aloha shirts, and "Duke's Pineapple" is among the best-known examples. The design became widely recognized in connection with the 1953 motion picture From Here to Eternity, helping establish it as one of the most celebrated pineapple patterns in the history of Hawaiian shirting.

Its lasting appeal comes from the combination of a distinctly Hawaiian subject, a strong mid-century graphic composition, and a color treatment that works naturally with the drape and movement of rayon fabric. The design remains visually expressive while retaining the refined character associated with collectible vintage Aloha shirts.

Pattern Placement and Individual Variation:

Because the shirt is made from an all-over printed fabric, the exact placement of the pineapple motifs will vary depending on where each garment panel is cut from the cloth. As a result, the position of the design on the collar, front panels, sleeves, back, and pockets may differ from the garment shown in the product photographs.

These differences are a normal result of the cutting process and make the pattern arrangement of each shirt slightly individual. Material characteristics, sewing, pressing, and finishing may also produce minor variations in the actual garment measurements.

Product Description

Fabric / Material

The body fabric is made from 100% cotton medium-weight circular-knit jersey. The garment is finished with a garment-dye process, also known as product dyeing or after-dyeing, which gives the fabric a naturally aged color tone and a slightly faded, vintage-inspired appearance from the beginning.

The jersey has a substantial medium-weight feel with enough body to give the shirt a solid presence, while still retaining the natural softness and flexibility of cotton. The fabric surface is not overly smooth or flat. Instead, it shows subtle vertical texture, fine yarn irregularity, slight slub-like variation, and faint nep-like character. These small surface variations give the fabric a more organic and dimensional appearance, helping the shirt avoid the flat, uniform look often associated with modern mass-produced jersey.

Although the fabric has a firm and substantial hand, it remains comfortable for casual wear. Through repeated wear and washing, the cotton jersey will continue to soften and develop more character, allowing the texture and color to age naturally over time.

Circular-Knit Tubular Body Construction

This T-shirt is made with a circular-knit tubular body. The torso is knitted in a tube shape rather than being cut from flat fabric and sewn together at the sides. As a result, the body has no side seams, creating the classic “tubular body” construction often associated with vintage athletic T-shirts, military undershirts, and older American casual knitwear.

Because there are no side seams along the torso, the shirt has a clean, uninterrupted body structure and a smooth feel against the skin. The absence of side seams also reduces side-seam bulk and friction, contributing to a more comfortable wearing experience. Visually, the tubular construction gives the shirt a traditional, old-style appearance while supporting a simple and natural drape through the body.

Garment-Dyed Finish

After the T-shirt is fully sewn, it is garment-dyed as a finished product. This process allows the dye to settle naturally into the fabric, ribbing, seams, and edges, creating subtle tonal variation and a broken-in appearance that cannot be fully reproduced by using pre-dyed fabric alone.

The garment-dye finish gives the shirt a muted, slightly faded color tone with a dry, vintage-like atmosphere. It also helps the fabric feel more familiar and comfortable from the start. Because the garment is dyed and finished after sewing, much of the initial shrinkage has already been reduced, helping the size and fit remain relatively stable after purchase. However, as with all cotton knitwear, slight natural changes may still occur with repeated washing and wear.

Fit and Silhouette

The silhouette is cleaner and more compact than many traditional American tubular T-shirts. It is designed with a slim body, a shorter body length, and shorter sleeves, giving the shirt a neat and balanced appearance. This trim, modernized fit helps the T-shirt work well as everyday casual wear while still preserving the character of vintage American military and athletic T-shirts.

Rather than having an oversized or boxy shape, the shirt is cut to sit cleanly on the body. The result is a refined casual silhouette with a classic feel, making it easy to pair with jeans, chinos, fatigue pants, shorts, or other heritage-inspired casual clothing.

Neckline Construction

The neckline is based on a classic crew neck and finished with binder-neck construction using rib fabric. Unlike a simpler collar construction where the rib is merely attached to the body, the binder-neck method wraps the cut edge of the body fabric with ribbing and secures it with double stitching.

This construction reinforces the neckline from both the inside and outside, helping reduce stretching, twisting, and shape distortion over time. It also gives the neck opening a more stable and durable structure, which is especially important for a T-shirt designed to reflect the functional character of vintage athletic and military garments.

Seam Construction

The shoulder seams, armholes, sleeve openings, and bottom hem are finished with single-stitch sewing. This restrained sewing specification gives the shirt a clean, simple, and understated appearance. Rather than looking overly modern or heavily engineered, the single-stitch finish helps preserve the quiet, old-style character of the garment.

The overall sewing is simple but carefully executed, supporting the shirt's vintage-inspired design without unnecessary decorative construction. This balance of plainness and precision is part of the appeal of TOYS McCOY's reproduction-oriented approach.

Print Construction

The chest graphic is printed with a slightly glossy, rubber-like ink. The print has a denser surface presence than a fully absorbed matte print, giving the “U.S. MARINES” graphic a strong visual character while still fitting naturally with the garment-dyed fabric.

A distinctive feature of this print is that it has been designed so the graphic can be faintly seen from the reverse side of the fabric. This is an intentional reproduction detail inspired by the way the T-shirt appears in Taxi Driver, where Travis Bickle wears the shirt inside out and the print shows through from the opposite side. The faint reverse-side show-through is therefore not a flaw, but a deliberate design element created to reproduce the film's visual atmosphere.

Taxi Driver Film Reference

The graphic design is based on the “U.S. MARINES” T-shirt worn by Robert De Niro as Travis Bickle in Taxi Driver. In the film, Travis Bickle wears a U.S. Marines T-shirt that refers to his background as a Vietnam veteran. In the memorable training scene, the shirt is worn inside out, allowing the graphic to appear in a ghosted, reversed manner through the fabric.

TOYS McCOY has recreated not only the graphic motif itself, but also the particular visual effect of the print showing faintly through from the reverse side. This gives the shirt a stronger connection to the film than a standard military-style printed T-shirt and adds a layer of cinematic and collectible appeal to the garment.

Non-Reversible Note

Please note that this T-shirt is not constructed as a true reversible garment. The reverse-side print effect is included as a design detail to reference the way the shirt appears in the film, but the shirt itself is not designed as a two-sided reversible T-shirt.

To support the film-inspired look, the size label is not attached at the back of the neck, but placed at the hem area instead. This allows the shirt to better reference the inside-out appearance seen in the film. However, the garment still includes care labeling and is fundamentally constructed as a standard single-face T-shirt. Please understand this as a film-based reproduction detail rather than a functional reversible specification.

Collection Context

This model is part of the TOYS McCOY Hollywood Legend collection, a series that reinterprets memorable garments associated with classic American film history through TOYS McCOY's reproduction-wear perspective. Rather than treating the design as a simple movie graphic, the brand applies period-aware fabric selection, body construction, dyeing, print treatment, silhouette balance, and finishing details to create a wearable modern product with a strong vintage and cinematic identity.

The result is a T-shirt that combines film culture, military-inspired graphic design, Japanese craftsmanship, and classic American casualwear references. It can be appreciated both as a collectible piece connected to Taxi Driver and as a well-made everyday T-shirt with authentic vintage-inspired character.

Overall Character

This T-shirt brings together a circular-knit tubular body, garment-dyed cotton jersey, binder-neck construction, single-stitch sewing, a compact modern silhouette, and a film-specific “U.S. MARINES” graphic. Each element contributes to the overall balance of authenticity, wearability, and visual character.

With its understated vintage texture, distinctive graphic treatment, and TOYS McCOY's careful attention to detail, this piece offers more than a standard printed T-shirt. It is a thoughtfully made graphic tee that reflects the atmosphere of classic American military and athletic wear while carrying the narrative presence of one of the most iconic costumes in American film history.

Model name:
TMC2624 TOYS McCOY 19"NY"76 Tee "U.S. Marines" (Successor model to TMC2515)

Care Instructions and Technical Explanation (Garment Label Details)

Hand Wash Only
Hand washing is recommended to reduce mechanical stress on the fabric, seams, and printed graphics. This gentle method helps maintain the natural hand feel of the cotton and prevents unnecessary abrasion that may occur during machine washing.

Do Not Bleach
Bleaching agents can damage cotton fibers and cause discoloration, particularly on dyed fabrics and printed areas. Avoiding bleach helps preserve the original color tone and overall fabric strength.

Cool Iron (Use a Pressing Cloth)
If ironing is necessary, use a low-temperature (cool) iron setting and always place a pressing cloth between the iron and the garment. This prevents direct heat contact, protecting the fabric surface, printed graphics, and stitching from heat damage, shine, or scorching. Ironing from the reverse side is also recommended for added protection.

Do Not Dry Clean
Dry cleaning solvents are not suitable for this garment, as they may negatively affect the cotton fibers, print quality, and sewn construction. Wet care methods are preferred to maintain authenticity and material integrity.

Dry in Shade
Air drying in the shade helps prevent color fading and fabric deterioration caused by prolonged exposure to direct sunlight. This is especially important for garments with vintage-inspired dyes and graphics.

Unlike a simpler collar construction where the rib is merely attached to the body, the binder-neck method wraps the cut edge of the body fabric with ribbing and secures it with double stitching.

This construction reinforces the neckline from both the inside and outside, helping reduce stretching, twisting, and shape distortion over time. It also gives the neck opening a more stable and durable structure, which is especially important for a T-shirt designed to reflect the functional character of vintage athletic and military garments.

Seam Construction

The shoulder seams, armholes, sleeve openings, and bottom hem are finished with single-stitch sewing. This restrained sewing specification gives the shirt a clean, simple, and understated appearance. Rather than looking overly modern or heavily engineered, the single-stitch finish helps preserve the quiet, old-style character of the garment.

The overall sewing is simple but carefully executed, supporting the shirt's vintage-inspired design without unnecessary decorative construction. This balance of plainness and precision is part of the appeal of TOYS McCOY's reproduction-oriented approach.

Print Construction

The chest graphic is printed with a slightly glossy, rubber-like ink. The print has a denser surface presence than a fully absorbed matte print, giving the “U.S. MARINES” graphic a strong visual character while still fitting naturally with the garment-dyed fabric.

A distinctive feature of this print is that it has been designed so the graphic can be faintly seen from the reverse side of the fabric. This is an intentional reproduction detail inspired by the way the T-shirt appears in Taxi Driver, where Travis Bickle wears the shirt inside out and the print shows through from the opposite side. The faint reverse-side show-through is therefore not a flaw, but a deliberate design element created to reproduce the film's visual atmosphere.

Taxi Driver Film Reference

The graphic design is based on the “U.S. MARINES” T-shirt worn by Robert De Niro as Travis Bickle in Taxi Driver. In the film, Travis Bickle wears a U.S. Marines T-shirt that refers to his background as a Vietnam veteran. In the memorable training scene, the shirt is worn inside out, allowing the graphic to appear in a ghosted, reversed manner through the fabric.

TOYS McCOY has recreated not only the graphic motif itself, but also the particular visual effect of the print showing faintly through from the reverse side. This gives the shirt a stronger connection to the film than a standard military-style printed T-shirt and adds a layer of cinematic and collectible appeal to the garment.

Non-Reversible Note

Please note that this T-shirt is not constructed as a true reversible garment. The reverse-side print effect is included as a design detail to reference the way the shirt appears in the film, but the shirt itself is not designed as a two-sided reversible T-shirt.

To support the film-inspired look, the size label is not attached at the back of the neck, but placed at the hem area instead. This allows the shirt to better reference the inside-out appearance seen in the film. However, the garment still includes care labeling and is fundamentally constructed as a standard single-face T-shirt. Please understand this as a film-based reproduction detail rather than a functional reversible specification.

Collection Context

This model is part of the TOYS McCOY Hollywood Legend collection, a series that reinterprets memorable garments associated with classic American film history through TOYS McCOY's reproduction-wear perspective. Rather than treating the design as a simple movie graphic, the brand applies period-aware fabric selection, body construction, dyeing, print treatment, silhouette balance, and finishing details to create a wearable modern product with a strong vintage and cinematic identity.

The result is a T-shirt that combines film culture, military-inspired graphic design, Japanese craftsmanship, and classic American casualwear references. It can be appreciated both as a collectible piece connected to Taxi Driver and as a well-made everyday T-shirt with authentic vintage-inspired character.

Overall Character

This T-shirt brings together a circular-knit tubular body, garment-dyed cotton jersey, binder-neck construction, single-stitch sewing, a compact modern silhouette, and a film-specific “U.S. MARINES” graphic. Each element contributes to the overall balance of authenticity, wearability, and visual character.

With its understated vintage texture, distinctive graphic treatment, and TOYS McCOY's careful attention to detail, this piece offers more than a standard printed T-shirt. It is a thoughtfully made graphic tee that reflects the atmosphere of classic American military and athletic wear while carrying the narrative presence of one of the most iconic costumes in American film history.

Model name:
TMC2624 TOYS McCOY 19"NY"76 Tee "U.S. Marines" (Successor model to TMC2515)

Care Instructions and Technical Explanation (Garment Label Details)

Hand Wash Only
Hand washing is recommended to reduce mechanical stress on the fabric, seams, and printed graphics. This gentle method helps maintain the natural hand feel of the cotton and prevents unnecessary abrasion that may occur during machine washing.

Do Not Bleach
Bleaching agents can damage cotton fibers and cause discoloration, particularly on dyed fabrics and printed areas. Avoiding bleach helps preserve the original color tone and overall fabric strength.

Cool Iron (Use a Pressing Cloth)
If ironing is necessary, use a low-temperature (cool) iron setting and always place a pressing cloth between the iron and the garment. This prevents direct heat contact, protecting the fabric surface, printed graphics, and stitching from heat damage, shine, or scorching. Ironing from the reverse side is also recommended for added protection.

Do Not Dry Clean
Dry cleaning solvents are not suitable for this garment, as they may negatively affect the cotton fibers, print quality, and sewn construction. Wet care methods are preferred to maintain authenticity and material integrity.

Dry in Shade
Air drying in the shade helps prevent color fading and fabric deterioration caused by prolonged exposure to direct sunlight. This is especially important for garments with vintage-inspired dyes and graphics.

Sugar Cane Men's 11oz Blue Denim Work Shorts - High-Rise Relaxed Straight Fit Knee-Length Button-Fly Shorts - Made in Japan (SC52565 421A One-Wash)

Sugar Cane

These men's denim work shorts are made in Japan by Sugar Cane, the vintage-inspired American workwear label of Toyo Enterprises, known for its careful craftsmanship and attention to authentic detail. Inspired by classic American work-pants styling, this pair is made from 11-ounce blue denim and tailored in an easy-to-wear knee-length silhouette suitable for warmer weather. Finished with Sugar Cane's signature workwear details throughout, these shorts combine a vintage-inspired casual look with practical everyday wearability, making them easy to incorporate into a modern casual wardrobe.

Size and Fit Guide:

Gender: Men.

Our model is wearing a tagged size 30. He stands 5'9" (175 cm) tall, weighs 127 lbs (58 kg), and has a chest measurement of 36 inches (91 cm). His usual size in U.S. denim is W29.

Fit: These shorts feature a classic relaxed straight fit with a high rise, a button fly, and an easy-to-wear knee-length silhouette. The shape is neither too slim nor too loose, giving them a balanced, classic profile. This garment has been pre-washed to reduce shrinkage and provide a more comfortable feel from the beginning. To ensure the best fit, please refer to the actual garment measurements listed below. All measurements are taken with the garment laid flat and are provided in both centimeters and inches. [Actual Garment Measurements]

For additional reference, the actual garment measurements are provided below. For a more accurate sense of fit, please use these measurements as a reference and compare them with a similar pair of shorts or pants you already own.

Product Description

Fabric

The fabric is a 100% cotton 11-ounce lightweight blue denim. It is woven on a shuttle loom using rope-dyed indigo yarns for the warp and gray yarns for the weft. The surface shows subtle yarn irregularities, fine natural hairiness, and a slightly uneven texture that are characteristic of traditional denim fabrics. Because the gray weft yarns subtly show through on the face of the fabric, the denim has a natural heathered cast and a slightly dry, workwear-like appearance.

Unlike modern denim fabrics that are often produced for maximum uniformity and smoothness, this fabric has a more rustic and dimensional texture. The combination of rope-dyed indigo warp yarns, gray weft yarns, and shuttle-loom weaving gives the fabric a classic blue denim character with depth and visual variation. With regular wear, the indigo surface will gradually develop fading, contrast, and a more personalized patina, allowing the shorts to age in a way unique to the wearer.

The garment has been one-washed. This process helps reduce most initial shrinkage while giving the fabric a more comfortable and wearable hand from the beginning.

Fit and Silhouette

The silhouette is designed with a high rise and a relaxed straight fit, giving the shorts a classic workwear profile. The fit is neither overly slim nor excessively loose, offering a comfortable, balanced shape with enough room through the top block and thigh. The length falls around the knee, creating a practical knee-length proportion that is easy to wear in warmer weather while still retaining the appearance of traditional work pants.

Front Closure

The front is constructed with a traditional button fly. A total of five metal buttons are used, including the waistband top button. The top button features the SUGAR CANE brand logo, while the buttons concealed inside the fly are metal donut buttons, a detail commonly associated with vintage workwear and denim trousers. The button-fly placket is also carefully constructed. Each buttonhole section on the fly is separated by individual rows of stitching, reinforcing the placket and helping maintain structure around each buttonhole. This detail adds durability to a high-stress area while giving the front closure a more authentic, workwear-oriented construction. The result is a front closure that enhances the vintage appearance of the shorts while also providing a firm and practical build.

Pocket Construction

The pocket layout is based on classic workwear utility. The front has slanted hand pockets on both sides, shaped for easy access. Above the right front pocket is a shallow utility pocket with a top-opening design. The back is equipped with large patch pockets on both sides, providing practical storage capacity while reinforcing the rugged appearance of the garment.

The front pocket bags are made with cotton pocketing cloth, and the lower portion of each pocket bag is woven more densely than the upper portion. This denser pocketing is used in the area most likely to receive stress from stored items, repeated hand movement, friction, and the weight of small objects. By strengthening the lower pocket-bag section, the construction improves durability and abrasion resistance in a part of the garment that is usually hidden from view but important for long-term wear.

The back patch pockets also include reinforcement on the inside lower section. This reinforcement cloth helps support the bottom of the pocket, where stress, weight, and friction tend to concentrate. On the outside of the garment, this internal reinforcement is visible as a horizontal line of stitching across the middle portion of the back pocket. Although it appears as a subtle design detail from the exterior, it is structurally functional and reflects the practical construction principles of traditional workwear.

Tool Details

In addition to the main pockets, the shorts feature a tool pocket on the right leg and a hammer loop on the left leg. These details are derived from classic work pants originally designed for carrying tools and small work items. On this pair, they add both functional utility and visual authenticity, strengthening the rugged character of the shorts without making them difficult to wear as everyday casual clothing.

Labels and Vintage-Inspired Trims

The label and trim details are also designed with vintage workwear in mind. A SUGAR CANE brand label is sewn onto the left back pocket, while a cloth patch is placed on the right side of the waistband. A size tag is inserted into the seam below the right back pocket, adding another workwear-style detail to the rear view of the garment.

Inside the left back pocket, a union-style tag is sewn in place. This type of label is often referred to as a union ticket or guarantee ticket and is a detail commonly found on vintage workwear, work shirts, and denim garments. Historically, such labels could indicate a union-related manufacturing background or quality assurance. In modern reproduction clothing, they serve as a period-correct design element that helps express the atmosphere and historical context of earlier American workwear. On this garment, the tag is not merely decorative; it helps reinforce the vintage workwear concept of the piece.

Sewing and Reinforcement Details

The waistband is equipped with five belt loops. The outseams, inseams, and back rise seam are sewn with triple-needle stitching, a durable construction method often associated with workwear garments. The main stitching is done in a white-tone thread, which stands out against the blue denim and emphasizes the garment's workwear construction.

Green reinforcement stitching is used at selected stress points, including the pocket openings and belt-loop areas. These contrast reinforcement stitches add both visual character and functional strength to areas that are subject to repeated pulling, movement, and wear. The combination of white stitching, green reinforcement stitching, triple-needle seams, and reinforced pocket construction gives the shorts a detailed and authentic workwear finish.

A vintage-style flasher is attached to the right back pocket with staples. This flasher is intended as a removable store-display detail and should be removed before wear. Together with the labels, pocket construction, contrast stitching, and workwear hardware, it contributes to the classic Sugar Cane presentation and enhances the overall vintage-inspired appearance of the garment.

Summary

This pair combines the easy wearability of 11-ounce lightweight denim with the durable construction and practical details of traditional American workwear. Although designed as warm-weather shorts, the garment is built with attention to fabric character, sewing specifications, hardware, labels, pocket reinforcement, and utility details. With wear, the denim will continue to develop more depth, fading, and character, making these Sugar Cane work shorts a piece that can be enjoyed not only for their immediate comfort, but also for the way they age over time.

Machine wash on a very gentle cycle with water temperature not exceeding 30°C / 86°F.
Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach.
Do not tumble dry.
Line dry in the shade.
Professional dry cleaning with petroleum solvent is allowed, mild process only.

Important Indigo Dye Notice

This product is made with indigo-dyed denim. Indigo dye is known for developing beautiful fading and character with wear, but excess dye on the surface of the fabric may rub off more easily, especially while the garment is still new. This natural characteristic of indigo denim is often referred to as crocking or color transfer.

Until the garment has been worn and washed several times, please avoid pairing it with light-colored clothing, bags, shoes, furniture, car seats, or other items that may be affected by color transfer. We also recommend washing this item separately from other garments.

When washing, please separate it from other items, as dye migration may occur. Do not use bleach, a clothes dryer, or hot water. Please avoid soaking the garment for a long period of time, and do not leave it wet or folded together with other items, as the dye may bleed or transfer while damp. - This T-shirt is made from 100% cotton tubular-knit jersey weighing approximately 6.0 oz. The fabric has a substantial medium-weight character: it is noticeably more substantial than a lightweight undershirt-style jersey, but it is not excessively thick or rigid. The knit provides enough body to give the garment a defined appearance while retaining the softness, flexibility, and breathability expected from a comfortable everyday cotton T-shirt.

Ring-Spun Cotton Yarn:
- The jersey is knitted from ring-spun cotton yarn. In ring spinning, cotton fibers are drawn out and twisted together to form a continuous yarn. This traditional spinning method contributes to a soft hand, natural surface character, and a subtly textured appearance. Rather than creating an overly smooth or completely uniform surface, the yarn allows the cotton fibers to retain a modest degree of natural variation and light surface hairiness. These qualities complement the vintage-inspired character of the garment while preserving a comfortable feel against the skin.

Fabric Texture and Surface Character:
- The surface of the jersey has a restrained but noticeable texture. Fine vertical knit wales appear across the fabric, creating subtle depth and preventing the surface from looking overly flat. Slight irregularities, fine slub-like variations, and light surface hairiness can also be seen throughout the knit. These characteristics are intentionally described as subtle: the fabric does not have an exaggeratedly rough or heavily uneven appearance. Instead, it offers a quiet, naturally varied texture that recalls the understated character of vintage cotton T-shirts.

Tubular-Knit Body Construction:
- The torso is constructed from a tubular-knit body panel with no side seams. Instead of cutting separate front and back sections and joining them together along the sides, the main body is knitted as a continuous tube. This construction removes the seams that would otherwise run vertically along the sides of the torso. The result is a clean, uninterrupted appearance and a comfortable fit with fewer stitched areas in direct contact with the body.

One-Wash Finish:
- The garment has been given a one-wash finish during production. This initial washing process helps settle the cotton jersey and reduce the amount of major shrinkage that might otherwise occur after the first home laundering. As a result, the T-shirt can be worn with a comparatively stable fit from the beginning. Some additional dimensional change may still occur with repeated washing, particularly if the garment is exposed to hot water or machine drying. To help maintain its shape and measurements, follow the care instructions and avoid tumble drying.

Silhouette and Sleeve Construction:
- This T-shirt follows a classic short-sleeve silhouette with set-in sleeves. Each sleeve is attached around a defined armhole seam, producing a conventional shoulder line rather than the diagonal seam arrangement found on raglan-sleeve garments. The proportions are intentionally straightforward and restrained, allowing the quality of the jersey and the construction details to remain the primary focus. The overall appearance is clean and traditional rather than oversized or heavily stylized.

Collar and Neckline Construction:
- The neckline is finished with a ribbed crew neck using binder-neck and bound collar construction. In this method, the edge of the body fabric is enclosed within the folded collar rib and secured with double-needle stitching, creating a durable and structurally stable neck finish. In addition to its functional benefits, this construction also contributes to the robust appearance often associated with vintage-inspired athletic T-shirts.

Sleeve Cuffs and Bottom Hem Construction:
- The sleeve openings and bottom hem are finished with double-needle stitching. Two parallel rows of stitches secure the folded edges, reinforcing areas that are subject to repeated movement, wear, and laundering. On the interior, the raw edges are neatly overlocked, also known as serged, to help prevent fraying and improve long-term seam stability. This finishing method keeps the construction relatively flat and unobtrusive, allowing the jersey to retain its natural flexibility and comfort.

Pocket Construction:
- The left chest is fitted with a patch pocket made from the same cotton jersey as the body. Rather than using a simple square shape, the pocket is finished with a pointed lower edge, giving it a subtly defined five-sided profile. This modest geometric detail adds visual interest while preserving the understated appearance of a traditional American pocket T-shirt. - This T-shirt is designed as a simple pull-over garment with no buttons, zippers, or other closure systems. product.title: Ultimate Pima Tsuriami Crewneck T-Shirt - Khaki
product.body_html:
As Wonder Looper grows and evolves, it only makes sense that they would broaden their horizons into fabric like Ultimate Pima. This organic cotton falls within the top 1% of US Cotton production, garnering the name. We've always had a huge crush on Pima cotton for its cool-feeling nature and absolutely supple hand feel. This variation of crew neck is quite a bit lighter than its "Heavyweight" predecessor for wearing all year round. It is the lightest garment in the lineup at 200gsm and feels closer to a "standard" tee, without any of the standard qualities. These are once again woven on the century-old Tsuriami machines the brand has prided itself on continuing to utilize in each production run. While this machine normally creates texture in a garment, this baby is all smooth. Pima is incredible in that way - it's so soft and comfy yet stronger than 99% of the cotton on the market.

product.title: Double Heavyweight Crewneck T-Shirt - Heather Grey
product.body_html:
We got in on Wonder Looper before the brand had a website. The owners asked whether we wanted some of the heaviest knits being made anywhere, and that is a short conversation. Heavyweight tees are familiar ground for us and for most of the people who shop here, but these sit in a different category. The jersey runs 409gsm, or 12.1oz per square yard, roughly double what the industry calls heavyweight, and the surprise is that it still drapes. A fabric this dense could easily hang like cardboard. Instead, the weight pulls it down into a clean line off the shoulders. Knitting it this way takes time. The jersey is circular knit in Japan at low tension, which is where the uneven surface texture comes from, the kind of irregular face that makes a vintage tee look like a vintage tee rather than a printed blank. Construction holds up its end. The collar is a binder neck with ribbing, bound rather than simply set in, so it keeps its shape through years of pulling the shirt over your head. The side seams are joined on a union special flat seam machine, which butts the panels together and stitches them flat so there is no ridge running down your ribs. Cut and sewn in Japan. We were one of the first shops in the country to carry these. They sold out, we reordered, and they sold out again.

  • 409gsm / 12.1oz per square yard
  • 100% cotton Japanese jersey
  • Circular knit with uneven surface texture
  • Binder neck ribbed collar
  • Union special flat side seams
  • Cut and sewn in Japan

product.title: Zip Hoodie - Double Heavyweight French Terry - Navy
product.body_html:
Wakayama sits at the center of Japan's knitting industry, and it is where this French terry is made, run on circular knitting machines at a low 10 gauge. Fewer needles around the cylinder means heavier yarn and a coarser, more irregular surface, and it means the knitting takes its time. What comes off the machine lands at roughly twice the weight of a standard heavyweight knit, with large, soft loops covering the entire inside face. From there, the interior is lightly brushed, just enough to puff those loops into a half-fleece that holds warmth close while leaving the terry structure intact, so the inside reads fuller and softer and still looks like the knit it is. The finished garment is rinse-washed and pre-shrunk to settle the fabric and keep further shrinkage at home to a minimum. Raglan sleeves let the shoulders move freely under all that weight, and ribbed panels run down the sides into the cuffs and hem to give the knit structure and hold its shape. Flat-seam construction keeps the joins smooth against the skin and gives the piece a clean, finished look throughout. Down the front runs a heavy-gauge two-way Waldes zipper, a name that traces back to the early decades of the zipper trade, and the two-way slider lets the hem open up while the top stays closed. A drawstring hood and split hand-warmer pockets complete the front.

product.body_html:
Waffle knits earn their place in cold weather through geometry. The honeycomb structure raises and recesses the surface into hundreds of small pockets, and each one holds a little air against the body, which is why waffle insulates while still breathing freely and why it spent a century as the standard for thermal underwear before anyone wore it on the outside. orSlow knits this one in Japan at 5.8oz with a soft hand and a good amount of give, helped along by the single percent of polyurethane blended into the cotton body, which lets the knit stretch as you move and return to shape afterward. The texture is the point as much as the warmth here, breaking up the surface of an outfit in a way a flat jersey leaves alone. Ribbing finishes the collar and the sleeve ends in 100% cotton. One thing worth knowing before the first wash: the fabric is not pre-rinsed, so orSlow expects roughly 3 to 4% shrinkage, which works out to about half an inch to an inch across most dimensions and a little more through the length.

product.title: 11oz - Work Shirt Roll-Dyed Selvedge Canvas - Dark Brown
product.body_html:
Dye behaves differently depending on when it meets the cloth. Rogue Territory sends this 11oz Japanese selvedge canvas through a roll dye in its raw state, which lays the brown onto the surface of the yarns rather than driving it all the way to the core. That is the same principle behind a good pair of raw jeans, and it sets the shirt up to shed pigment slowly, lightening at the elbows, the cuffs, the placket, and anywhere else the fabric moves against itself. The dyeing happens in Los Angeles, a short trip from the floor where the shirts are sewn. Once construction is finished, each piece goes through an industrial wash that pulls some of the surface dye back off, so the shirt arrives with a worn-in patina already started and a hand that has lost its stiffness. The wash also means the brown stays where it belongs, so you can wear it over anything. Inside, contrast red chain stitching runs the seams and ties back to the bold red selvedge ID, and the placket is cut on the selvedge so that finished edge faces out every time the shirt is open. The canvas carries a natural stretch that lets it relax into shape quickly. Dual chest pockets, triple-needle chainstitched seams with run-off, a herringbone locker loop, and antiqued brass snaps handle the rest.

The shape takes its cues from vintage knitwear: a boxy body, a hem that stops short, shoulders dropped past the natural line, and a v-neck opening cut a little lower than usual. Chunky ribbing runs the cuffs, the hem, and a 1.5" collar, giving the sweater enough structure at its edges to hold that boxy line rather than slumping. Alpaca carries the warmth at 60% of the blend, wool brings the resilience, and it all gets knit in Peru.

product.title: Classic Cardigan - Pewter Alpaca
product.body_html:
Alpacas come in two types, and the difference shows up in the fleece. Huacaya fleece grows with a crimp that gives it loft and a woolly look, while Suri fleece grows in long, straight locks that hang down the animal in ropes, closer to dreadlocks than to a sheep's coat. Those uncrimped fibers take light differently, which is where Suri gets its luster, and spun into yarn they leave a halo of fine hairs standing off the surface. Suri alpacas account for roughly 10% of the world's alpaca population, so the fleece is harder to come by and prized by the people who work with it. 3sixteen knits this season's Classic Cardigan from a Suri alpaca and wool blend in pewter, and the character of the fiber carries the piece: light and airy in the hand, hairy and textured across the surface, with a quiet sheen running through the color. The cut keeps its usual shape with a v-neck, raglan shoulder detailing worked into the front, ribbed cuffs and hem, and a simple collar, all of it finished with corozo buttons and knit in Peru.

product.title: 22oz - Elephant 2 Reborn Selvedge - Denim Jacket
product.body_html:
Some fabrics get talked about for a season. Elephant 2 has been talked about for years, long enough that Naked & Famous is now bringing it back for a third run on the strength of what people keep posting after wearing it, and this time the 22oz lands in jacket form. The weight is the first thing you notice. A 22oz Japanese selvedge arrives dense and rigid, and on a jacket that means it holds its own shape off the hanger and stands away from the body rather than draping over it. Heavy, uneven yarns run through the weave and leave ridges and raised slub across the surface, so there is real topography in the cloth from the start. That texture is what the fades eventually follow. Wear it and the denim begins softening in stages, loosening first at the elbows, the cuffs, and the collar fold while the indigo pulls back from every high point in the weave. Rope dyeing leaves each yarn with a white core, and at this weight the breaking-in exposes those cores quickly, which is where the high contrast, the deep creasing, and the pronounced texture of a well-worn jacket all come from. A button front runs the placket, with flap pockets at the chest, slash pockets at the hands, and interior pocket bags inside. A 10oz natural vegetable-tanned leather patch sits at the back, heavy enough to earn its own patina, and tin hardware finishes the rest.

product.title: 270-60XX - 12oz Selvedge Denim - Just Right Straight
product.body_html:
American denim from the 1960s ran lighter than the heavyweight Japanese fabrics that later came to define the category, and the 270-60XX goes back to that reference point. ONI built this fabric with a 12.5oz American cloth of the era in mind, then wove and finished it in Japan at 12oz, which lands it at a weight you can wear in August and still get real fading out of by spring. The surface is where ONI's hand shows. Slub runs irregularly through the weave and the face stays naturally uneven, so there is depth in the denim from the first time you put it on rather than something that only arrives after a year of wear. Those same irregularities are what the fades eventually follow, pulling the indigo back along the high points of the weave and leaving a pattern that belongs to one pair only. Copper rivets, a button fly, and a leather patch handle the hardware, and a single wash means the shrink is already out of it.

product.title: 900HM-60XX - 12oz "Handmade" Selvedge Denim - Wide Straight
product.body_html:
Before automated sewing machines took over the factory floor and rivets became the standard answer to a stress point, a pair of work pants got its strength from the hands that built it and the stitches those hands put down. The 900HM-60XX is ONI's reconstruction of that approach, and the HM in the name stands for handmade. Rows of stitching pile up where a later pair would simply place a rivet, the seams are flat-felled rather than chainstitched lap seams, the bar tacks run linear, and the belt loops are the Banzai type, named for the way their raised ends look like arms thrown up in celebration. Every one of those choices slows the sewing down and leaves the finished pair with the slightly irregular, squared-off character of old workwear. The fabric looks back to American denim of the 1960s, woven and finished in Japan at 12oz with an uneven surface, subtle slub running through it, and the visual depth ONI has built its name on. That weight keeps the jeans wearable deep into warm weather while giving up none of the texture, and the irregularity of the weave means the fades will land differently on every pair.

product.title: Dehen for Dant - N-1 Waxed Deck Jacket - Hardtack, Kodiak
product.body_html:
The Dehen for Dant N-1 Waxed Deck Jacket returns in Hardtack and Kodiak, our own take on a tan waxed canvas we fell for last year and barely got to enjoy before it was gone. Rather than chase it, we worked with Dehen to develop our own interpretation, and it came out truly incredible. The finish is monochromatic, with the waxed shell, the mouton and even the canvas zipper pulls all living in the same warm family of tans, which carries the N-1 past vintage reproduction into something sleek, refined and modern. Hardtack takes its name from the dense ship's biscuit sailors lived on for months at sea, a fitting nod for a Navy deck jacket, while Kodiak is a rich, bear-brown mouton with real sheen. They sound like they belong together and look it even more, as if they were meant to be paired all along and we just got there first. It's a Dant exclusive with a custom Dant x Dehen label, in a color pairing that lives outside Dehen's regular lineup and only here.

The N-1 is the warmest jacket we carry, hands down. The body and collar are fully lined in genuine mouton, so a tee underneath is usually all it takes on the most frigid days, and the shearling is soft enough for bare skin with no itchies or scratchies. The 10 oz waxed canvas shell marbles from highs to lows as it creases, the kind of color shift that separates a great waxed garment from a flat one, and it only deepens as it picks up your own wear. Cuffs are 100% worsted wool knit on Dehen's 1940s machines in Portland, and a #10 army green brass zipper hides behind the six-button placket. The Navy first sent the N-1 to sea in WWII to keep deck crews warm on the North Atlantic, and 80-some years later this one is still more than up for the job.

product.title: 13oz - Foxfibre® Green Weft Selvedge - True Guy
product.body_html:
Iron is the quiet trick behind this fabric. Green FoxFibre® comes off the plant already carrying color, and treating it with iron, a mineral mordant that natural dyers have leaned on for centuries, sets off a reaction with the pigment already sitting inside the fiber rather than laying new color over the top of it. What comes out the other side is a deeper, steadier green-grey, and because the color lives in the fiber instead of coating it, washing and wear push the tone further along rather than stripping it away. Naked & Famous runs that weft against indigo rope-dyed warp yarns in a 13oz Japanese selvedge, which sets up the long game: as the indigo gives way at the knees and the seat, the green-grey underneath comes forward. Green is the difficult one in the FoxFibre® family. Sally Fox began selectively breeding naturally pigmented cotton in the 1980s to take chemical dyeing out of the equation, and the green variety she developed grows shorter fibers at much lower yields than the brown, which makes it harder to spin consistently and keeps the supply thin. For this denim the cotton is grown in the United States and the yarn is spun in Osaka, putting American organic agriculture and Japanese weaving on the same loom. A 5oz natural vegetable-tanned leather patch sits at the waistband, ready to darken and take on its own patina alongside the denim, with tin hardware and a button fly closing things out.

  • 100% organic cotton
  • Weft: 100% FoxFibre®, iron-mordanted
  • Indigo rope-dyed warp
  • Cotton grown in the United States, yarn spun in Osaka
  • 5oz natural vegetable-tanned leather patch
  • Button fly closure
  • Tin hardware
  • Made in Canada

product.title: Samurai Jeans S310XX19ozII 19oz Super Wide Jeans
product.body_html:
New for 2026, the 310 is now the widest silhouette Samurai Jeans makes, and the brand gave it its heaviest everyday denim to match. The fabric is Samurai’s 19oz selvedge, and the construction is worth understanding. The warp is a No. 5 uneven slub yarn spun from coarse, hard raw cotton with a high-twist method that deliberately pushes the surface toward rough and grainy; slub in a yarn this thick is hard to make look natural, and here it comes through as organic irregularity rather than a forced effect. The weft is a thick No. 4 yarn, which leaves the inside of the fabric softer against the skin while the outer face stays coarse and heavy. Firm in hand, it is built for high-contrast fades, and it comes one-washed.

The cut is a super wide straight with a deep, high rise (32 cm / 12.6" at the front on a 32), a very roomy top block and a leg that runs wide and straight to a 26 cm (10.2") opening. For all that width, the proportions have been drawn to avoid exaggeration: it reads as a wide jean, not a costume.

Specifications are the house standard, with a few things made for the model: “hinomaru” sunrise iron buttons, Samurai’s original rivets, a selvedge-cut coin pocket, the brand’s red and silver lamé selvedge ID, pocket bags jacquard-woven with “shogyo mujo” (諸行無常), the impermanence of all things, an original goatskin leather patch and flasher, the brand’s original back-pocket stitch and a rayon label. Unsanforized, 100% cotton, made in Japan.

Fit Notes: This model fits true to size for Samurai: the tagged size closely matches the actual waist measurement. Compared to most global American brands, sizing is similar or slightly smaller, so you may take the same size or one size up. The 310 is a super wide straight with a high rise a very roomy top block and a wide leg opening, so it is meant to be worn with room throughout. The denim is unsanforized but has been one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected; the waistband will stretch slightly with wear. We don’t recommend sizing down, as starting too tight may cause discomfort and alter the intended fit of the garment. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart to find your perfect size.

product.title: Samurai Jeans S0710XX-BOB 15oz "Aoki Tachikage" Black On Blue Slim Straight Jeans
product.body_html:
Aoki Tachikage — 青き太刀影, “Blue Blade Shadow” — is the image of a sword cutting through darkness and leaving a blue glint behind it, and the denim is built to do exactly that. On the hanger these jeans read as black-on-black. With wear they turn out to be two colors: the black is the surface, and the blue is what it was hiding.

The fabric works in layers. The warp is a #6 slub yarn that is first rope-dyed in indigo and then overdyed with sulphur black, a three-stage process that leaves black on top, indigo underneath and the natural white core at the center. As the pair breaks in, the sulphur black wears off the high points first, exposing the indigo; the indigo then fades in its own time toward the white core, so every worn area eventually shows three tones at once — black, exposed blue, and the pale core of the yarn. The weft is an uneven #6 yarn dyed sulphur black as well, which deepens the overall tone and fades to grey rather than white. At 15oz, the cloth has enough body to crease hard and hold the contrast, and the silver lamé selvedge — the brand’s nod to the samurai’s blade — runs the outseam.

The 710 is Samurai’s slim straight: a mid rise, a slim thigh and a leg that runs straight with a slight taper to a 19.5 cm (7.7") opening — the trimmest frame in the lineup for a fabric that fades this hard.

The details were drawn for this denim alone: a five-button fly in blue-coated metal embossed with the Samurai name, navy sewing thread throughout, jacquard pocket bags woven with a family-crest pattern, a selvedge-cut coin pocket and the brand’s goatskin leather patch. The denim is unsanforized and one-washed. 100% cotton. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: This model runs small: the waist measures about 1" under the tagged size. Compared to most global American brands, we recommend sizing up one from your usual size. The denim is unsanforized but has been one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected; the waistband will stretch slightly with wear. We don’t recommend sizing down, as starting too tight may cause discomfort and alter the intended fit of the garment. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart to find your perfect size.

product.title: Samurai Jeans S0510XXII 15oz "Otokogi" Regular Straight Jeans
product.body_html:
If one pair stands for Samurai Jeans, it is this one: the brand’s 15oz regular straight, cut in the denim the brand calls Otokogi. The yarn is a slubby #6 cotton thread spun with the small bits of cotton waste deliberately left in the mix, and the cloth is woven on vintage shuttle looms run to the edge of what they can take. What comes off the loom is rough in look and in hand, with neps and slub breaking the surface — and it is exactly that irregularity that produces the high-contrast fades this fabric is known for. The silver lamé selvedge runs the outseam, the brand’s reference to the Japanese sword.

The cut is vintage in feel without being a costume: a little room around the waist, a straight leg with a gentle taper to the hem, and a leg width that sits between slim and wide — the balance most people are looking for in a five-pocket jean.

The leather patch is exclusive to this model, drawn from the classic Samurai patch: the warriors Musashi and Kojiro, the moon, pine trees, a Shinto torii gate and Mt. Fuji, with two seagulls added to mark these jeans as the successor to the S0510XX. The rest of the hardware follows suit — iron “hinode” sunrise buttons, copper coin-shaped rivets, an exclusive flasher, and pocket bags jacquard-woven with “shogyo mujo” (諸行無常), “all things must pass” — a reminder stitched into a garment that will prove it. One-washed. 100% cotton. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: Samurai Jeans run small compared to most global American brands, so we recommend sizing up one from your usual size. The cut is a regular straight with a little room at the waist and a gentle taper to the hem. The denim has been one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected; the waistband will give slightly with wear. We don’t recommend sizing down, as starting too tight may cause discomfort and alter the intended fit of the garment. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart to find your perfect size.

product.title: Samurai Jeans SJ2PST-CREW Tubular Charcoal T-Shirt (2 Pack)
product.body_html:
Samurai's signature tubular two-pack T-shirts are cut from soft recycled #19 yarn cotton and feature a double-needle stitched binder neck that fits trim and hits high on the bicep — creating a flattering silhouette that looks clean on everyone.

The milled, two-needle binder neck ensures the collar withstands hard wear, and the T-shirts are crafted with the same level of expertise as the brand's celebrated denim. The cotton yarn is carefully knit on a tubular machine, resulting in a super soft midweight fabric with the seamless construction that Samurai is known for.

These T-shirts come in a pack of two and are perfect for wearing as standalone pieces during the summer or as undershirts throughout the rest of the year. The tubular construction using No.19 yarn offers a moderate thickness that makes the tees comfortable to wear even under a shirt in warm weather.

To withstand hard wear, the collar rib is finished with a highly durable two-needle binder neck construction. The pattern is designed with a fit that does not interfere with layering — making this a true everyday workhorse. The fabric has been one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected.

Fit Notes: These T-shirts run small. Compared to most global American brands, we recommend sizing up one from your usual size for a comfortable fit. As a reference, a Samurai size L fits closer to a standard American Medium. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart and comparing it with your best-fitting T-shirt to ensure the right fit.

product.title: Wonder Looper Pullover Crewneck 876gsm Double Heavyweight French Terry Oatmeal
product.body_html:
Eight hundred and seventy-six grams per square meter. At 876gsm — 25.8oz per square yard — this crewneck carries close to twice the fabric density of a standard heavyweight sweatshirt, and it is a different garment for it: warmer, more structured, with a weight on the shoulders that reads as substance rather than bulk. It is made in Wakayama, the Japanese city whose circular-knitting mills set the standard for this kind of fabric.

The cloth is a French terry developed for this piece, knitted on low-gauge (10G) circular machines so the face carries a subtly irregular texture with real depth. Inside, the terry forms large, plush loops that cushion the skin, and the surface has been lightly brushed for a half-fleece effect — the loops stay visible, but they are gently raised, so the interior feels softer and fuller while keeping the character of the knit.

The garment comes one-washed and pre-shrunk, which sets the fabric and keeps further shrinkage at home to a minimum. The cut is a modern athletic fit, with classic sweatshirt details: a ribbed binder collar with a vintage-style V-gusset, raglan sleeves for freedom through the shoulder, and ribbed side panels, cuffs and hem that give the body structure without restricting. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: This model fits true to size and runs slightly larger than most Japanese sweatshirts. We recommend taking your usual size for a comfortable fit. Compared to most global American brands, a Medium fits similarly to a standard Medium. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart and comparing it to your best-fitting shirt to find the perfect size.

product.title: Mooncastle Shetland Wool Crewneck Pullover Gold
product.body_html:
Shetland wool has always traded softness for character: a lofty, slightly hairy fiber with real warmth and the kind of durability that keeps a sweater in service for decades. Mooncastle's SW1 keeps that character and rounds off its edge by knitting the Shetland together with merino in an exclusive 100% wool blend — the body and resilience of the one, the softer hand of the other, in a fabric that feels light on the shoulders and holds heat the way a proper Shetland should.

The sweater is made by seamless whole-garment knitting: the body and sleeves come off the machine as a single piece, with no seams at the shoulders or sides to bulk up, rub, or give way. The result is a clean crew neck with ribbed cuffs and hem and an even drape all round. Gold is one of ten colors in the range, sitting between mustard and ochre, and it is a shade that reads well against denim and dark tailoring alike. As with all knitwear, allow a variation of 1–2 cm between pieces.

Mooncastle recommends dry cleaning; tumble drying and machine washing will shrink and distort the wool. Between wears, a soft brush keeps the surface tidy, any pills should be removed with a pill comb rather than pulled, and a day's rest after a day's wear will add years to the sweater. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: This sweater follows Japanese sizing and runs a bit small. Compared to most global American brands, we recommend sizing up one from your usual size for a comfortable fit — an L fits similarly to an American M. The knit is light and close to the body, with ribbed cuffs and hem that hold with a moderate grip, and knitwear can vary by 1–2 cm from piece to piece. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart and comparing it with your best-fitting garment to ensure the right fit.

product.title: Mooncastle 12G Lightweight Merino Wool Crewneck Pullover Sand Beige
product.body_html:
A crew neck reduced to what matters. Mooncastle, the Osaka knitwear house, makes this sweater from 100% superfine Australian merino — the finest grade of the fiber, which is why the surface has a soft sheen and a smooth, almost silky hand, and why it sits against bare skin with little of the itch coarser wool brings. It is knitted in a 12-gauge plain jersey: fine enough to go under a jacket or over a shirt without bulk, dense enough to hold real warmth and to last.

The shape is drawn to be worn, not noticed. Ribbed cuffs and hem hold with a moderate grip rather than pinching, and the body follows the torso in a clean line that works with tailoring as easily as with jeans and sneakers. Beige melange — a heathered, undyed-looking tone — was a color Mooncastle sold last year only in its own stores and at select Japanese stockists; it is now offered while stock lasts.

Care is simpler than most merino: machine washable on a gentle cycle, turned inside out in a mesh bag. Smooth out the creases while it is wet and dry it flat, or hung over a thick pole, and it keeps its shape. As with all knitwear, expect a variation of 1–2 cm between pieces. Made in Japan.

product.title: ONI Denim 275 20oz Awa Kakishibu x Kinari Regular Straight Jeans
product.body_html:
This rare collector’s edition from ONI features hand-dyed Awa kakishibu warp yarns and natural undyed (kinari) weft yarns, creating a warm, earthy tone with subtle depth and a soft, organic presence. Kakishibu is a traditional Japanese dye made from fermented persimmon tannin—historically used for textiles, wood, and paper— prized for the way it ages beautifully, darkening and developing character as it oxidizes with sunlight and wears.

The fabric is woven on antique shuttle looms at low tension. The result is a 20oz slubby denim with rich texture and slow, graceful fading that reflects the touch of the craftsperson. The kinari weft adds a natural warmth beneath the kakishibu-dyed warp, giving the denim a quiet, understated complexity that deepens with time and wear.

Cut in the ONI 275 Regular Straight fit, this pair offers a balanced silhouette with a comfortable rise and room throughout—versatile, classic, and easy to wear.

Fit Notes: These jeans have a standard sizing. We recommend choosing your usual size. However, as always, we recommend checking the size chart first to find your perfect size. The fabric is unsanforized, but the jeans have been one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected. The waist will experience the typical stretching seen in ONI denim due to the low tension weave, although not as much as the secret denim. Expect approximately 1 inches of stretching.

product.title: ONI Denim 03500-CHOL Olive Chino Cloth Coverall
product.body_html:
The same cloth as the 271 chinos, cut into a coverall. The fabric is ONI's 8oz vintage-style selvedge chino twill, with both warp and weft yarn-dyed olive so the color lives inside the thread: it holds better, reads deeper, and fades slowly and evenly into patina rather than contrast. Smooth on the inside and slightly rugged on the outside, the surface grows more uneven with every month of wear — which on a work jacket is the point.

The pattern is the classic coverall: a straight, roomy body that closes with a button placket, long enough at 76 cm (29.9") on a 42 to cover the hips, with a shoulder cut wide enough to go over a shirt and a sweater. Pockets do the work — two chest pockets, one of them with an internal pocket for anything that needs to stay put, and two large patch pockets at the hips.

Construction is ONI's: custom copper doughnut buttons down the front, clean stitching along the placket and seams, and the brand's signature details where the maker would put them. 100% cotton. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: This coverall fits true to size with a relaxed, roomy cut. Compared to most global American brands, a size 42 fits similarly to a standard Large. We recommend taking your usual size for a comfortable fit. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart and comparing it with your best-fitting jacket to ensure the right fit.

product.title: ONI Denim 271-SVCKB Just Right Straight Selvedge Chino Cloth Khaki Beige Jeans
product.body_html:
Chino cloth, made the way ONI makes denim. The 271-SVCKB is cut from an 8oz vintage-style selvedge chino twill in which both the warp and the weft are yarn-dyed khaki beige — the color sits inside the thread rather than on the surface, which gives the cloth stronger colorfastness, a warmer, deeper khaki, and a fade that comes slowly and evenly, as patina rather than contrast. The two faces of the fabric differ: smooth on the inside against the skin, slightly rugged on the outside, and the outside grows more uneven the longer it is worn.

The cut is ONI's Just Right Straight: the 270 pattern, adjusted here to the behavior of the chino cloth. It is a regular straight with a comfortable high rise (11.4" at the front on a 31–34) that sits a touch higher than the 288, more room through the thigh than the 288, and a leg that runs straight from the knee with a subtle taper to an 8.1" opening on a 31 — clean enough to read as straight. It is the most adaptable shape in the range, at home with boots, sneakers or dress shoes, and worn smart or casual without changing anything.

Construction follows the brand's five-pocket standard: ONI's branded copper doughnut buttons, hidden rivets on the back pockets, raised belt loops, a vegetable-tanned leather patch and a vintage white selvedge ID at the outseam. The fabric is unsanforized and one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected. Produced in very limited quantities. 100% cotton. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: This model fits true to size for ONI: the tagged size matches the actual waist measurement. Compared to most global American brands, sizing is similar or slightly smaller, so you may take the same size or one size up. The cut is a regular straight with a high rise, room through the thigh and a subtle taper to the leg opening. The chino twill is sanforized, so no further shrinkage is expected; the waistband will give slightly with wear. We don't recommend sizing down, as starting too tight may cause discomfort and alter the intended fit of the garment. As always, we strongly recommend checking our size chart to find your perfect size.

product.title: ONI Denim L722-12B "Ladies" 12oz Super Wide Straight Jeans
product.body_html:
The L722 is where ONI's women's line goes widest. Like the rest of the third Ladies capsule, it starts from a pattern drawn from a blank sheet for a woman's body rather than a scaled-down men's block — waist and rise balanced against each other, back pockets placed for a clean, vintage line — and then opens the leg as far as the range allows: a super wide straight that runs almost the same width from the thigh to the hem, a counterpart to the men's 222.

The denim is a 12oz selvedge woven on vintage shuttle looms from a mix of yarns in different thicknesses, which gives the cloth a light crunch and a hand that is firm yet supple — the texture and substance of Japanese denim at a weight that drapes in a leg this wide, where a heavier fabric would stand away from the body. It comes one-washed, ready to wear, and the deep indigo will fade slowly across a surface with plenty of room to show it.

The cut sits at a high rise (11.4" at the front on a size 1) with a wide top block, and the leg drops straight and full from a 12.6" thigh to an 11" opening on the same size; a deep cuff shows the selvedge and keeps the proportion in check. Construction is full ONI: custom copper doughnut buttons on a button fly, original punched rivets, a cowhide leather patch and the selvedge ID at the outseam, plus the women's line's quiet signature — purple thread at the coin-pocket opening and the inner bar tacks of the back pockets. 100% cotton. Made in Japan.

ONI makes the L722 in two versions, zip fly and button fly, and we stock the button-fly L722-12B. It is the more traditional construction — the one on every vintage pair this pattern looks back to — and the one that ages best: a button fly keeps the front flat and clean, never fails the way a zip can, and its placket fades and softens along with the rest of the jeans.

Fit Notes: This model fits true to size — we recommend taking your usual size. ONI's women's sizes run 0–4; as a guide, a size 1 measures 27.6" at the waist and corresponds roughly to a 25–26 in American brands, a size 2 (28.3") to a 26–27, and so on. The cut is a super wide straight with a high rise and a leg that stays almost the same width from a 12.6" thigh to an 11" opening, so it is meant to be worn with room throughout. The denim has been one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected. With regular wear, the waistband will stretch approximately 1 inch, allowing the fit to settle comfortably over time. product.title: ONI Denim 222 "Asphalt" 20oz Super Wide Straight Jeans
product.body_html:
Asphalt is the right name. Dark, coarse and flecked with white, the surface of this 20oz denim looks more like tarmac than cloth, and it is where Oishi-san takes the two things ONI is known for — slub and nep — as far as they go. The yarn is spun with extreme variation in thickness, so the weave comes out rugged and irregular, and it is peppered with white cotton neps, the knots of short fiber most mills remove, which break the dark indigo surface with pale flecks. Woven on a shuttle loom at ultra-low tension, with a dark indigo warp over a white weft, it is one of the most tactile denims ONI has produced, and it is made in very limited quantities.

At this weight the fabric starts stiff and stays that way for a while; the reward is fading with real depth, where the neps and slubs catch the wear first and the indigo breaks unevenly around them.

The 222 is the widest cut in ONI's lineup: a super wide straight with a high rise, a relaxed waist and seat, and a leg that runs in one clean line to the hem with no taper. It takes oversized styling while keeping classic proportions, and it works with boots, sneakers or sandals alike.

Construction is ONI's own: custom copper doughnut buttons and hardware, punched copper rivets with hidden rivets on the back pockets, heavy-duty bar tacks, raised belt loops, a peek-a-boo selvedge coin pocket, cotton-lined front pockets and a vegetable-tanned cowhide leather patch, with the red selvedge ID at the outseam. Unsanforized and one-washed, ready to wear from the box. 100% cotton. Made in Japan.

Fit Notes: This model fits true to size — we recommend taking your usual size. The 222 is a super wide straight with a high rise and no taper, so it is meant to sit with room from the waist down. The denim is unsanforized but has been one-washed, so no further shrinkage is expected. With regular wear, the waistband will stretch approximately 1 inch, allowing the fit to settle comfortably over time.
